2.0.0.en: God led His people by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, so they headed south toward the Red Sea (the Gulf of Aqaba) and went around the Seir mountain range, which lies in the land of Edom in the south of Palestine (maps 1, 13), and they began their journey in the wilderness of Sinai, to wander in it about 38 years, for the following reasons:

2.0.1.en: 1- The death of all the men from twenty years old and upward, who were the ones who murmured against God.

2.0.2.en: 2- The sons' experience of God's care, to confirm their faith in Him.

2.0.3.en: 3- The sons' estrangement from Egypt and its pagan worship, and the offering of worship to the one God in the Tabernacle of Meeting.

2.0.4.en: 4- Victory over some peoples such as Amalek, Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, to confirm their faith and prepare them to enter the Promised Land and gain victory over its peoples.

2.1.0.en: In the thirty-ninth year after their departure from Egypt, and after the death of the whole former generation, which had feared to carry out the Lord's command to enter the Promised Land, the Lord asked them to end their circling in the wilderness of Sinai and head north again toward the Promised Land, to begin carrying out the plan He had drawn for them to enter the land.

2.1.1.en: Our sojourn in the world is a temporary period, after which we return to heaven; therefore we must prepare throughout our life for our eternal life, and not indulge in the passing desires of the world nor be occupied with its labyrinths that never end, but always remember our only goal, which is to be with God on earth in preparation for being with Him forever in heaven.

2.2.0.en: In their course northward the people had to pass within the borders of the land of Esau, which is the region of Seir. The Edomites' fear of the congregation of Israel was due to their great number and to the awe God had cast upon His people which frightens enemies, and this reminds us of what is written in (Gen 35:5) concerning the awe of Jacob and his sons during their journeys. But God sternly warns them against attacking the Edomites, because He will not allow them to take the lands of the sons of Esau, since He had already given those lands to him as an inheritance (Josh 24:4). Here God explains to His children the reason for the prohibition; He is not content to issue commands to His beloved, but shares with them the knowledge of the reasons, and also teaches them:

2.2.1.en: 1- Not to be proud because the Edomites fear them and so rush to fight them, for this awe is a grace from God and not from themselves.

2.2.2.en: 2- To value the bond of brotherhood, because Esau is the brother of Jacob and so their descendants are brothers; although the sons of Esau had gone on to worship idols, the sons of Jacob should keep their love for them.

2.3.0.en: The Lord has blessed you in all the works of your hand: whether the raising of sheep or the wealth they took from the Egyptians (Ex 12:35, 36) and what they gained as spoil from Amalek after their victory over them (Ex 17:13). The Lord stressed that their dealing with the descendants of Esau should be with complete integrity and regard for their rights; if they bought anything from them, they should give them their due in the price and take nothing by force, knowing that in reality they had no need of this, for the Lord had provided them everything they needed during their journey in the wilderness, so the people felt no want or need of anything throughout the years of wandering. He gave them manna from heaven and water from the rock, yet did not prevent them from eating anything else they found in the wilderness; so if they wished to eat anything of the Edomites' produce, they were to buy it from them.

2.4.0.en: Elath: the present Eilat, at the northern end of the Gulf of Aqaba.

2.4.1.en: Ezion-geber: west of the port of Eilat, at present "Tell el-Kheleifeh" (map 1). The children of Israel tried to pass through the land of the Edomites, but they refused, so Israel did not fight them as God commanded, but went around their country from the plain extending west of the Dead Sea until they reached the north of the Gulf of Aqaba, then headed north to the east of the Dead Sea, to the land of Moab (Num 20:14-21).

2.4.2.en: May you value family relationships and kinship, and show love to everyone even if they have wronged you, for you love them for the sake of God, who gives you many blessings in your life.

2.5.0.en: Ar: one of the largest cities of Moab; it is also called Aroer and lies near its northern border, and was later called "Rabbath-moab"; it is now in ruins.

2.5.1.en: The Lord warned the children of Israel, on their way to the wilderness of Moab, not to stir up war against the Moabites, just as He had warned them before concerning the Edomites, and He also showed them the reason, which is that He had already given them their land as an inheritance, because Moab was the son of Lot by his elder daughter, and Lot was the righteous man whom God wished to honor in his descendants because he followed the way of the Lord and tormented his soul day and night by what he saw around him of the conduct of the wicked. In addition there was the kinship that links Lot to Abraham, their forefather, for he was his brother's son.

2.6.0.en: The Emims: they lived in the same region which the Moabites inhabited after them. They were a great and strong people and are also called Rephaims.

2.6.1.en: The Anakims: they are the sons of Anak who were described in the first chapter. The Anakims are one of the branches of the Rephaims.

2.6.2.en: He mentions the inhabitants of the land, who were the Emims, and likens them in their multitude and strength to the Anakims, and mentions that they are also called Rephaims because the Anakims are of the descendants of the Rephaims. God's mention of these ancient peoples who inhabited the land is not merely a historical account of the inhabitants of the land, but is to confirm and strengthen the faith of His people: just as these ancient peoples passed away, so God will remove the pagan inhabitants of the land of Canaan and drive them out from before His people.

2.7.0.en: The Horims: the original inhabitants of Mount Seir; the descendants of Esau destroyed them and dwelt in their place.

2.7.1.en: Just as the Book of Deuteronomy told us in the preceding verses the original inhabitants of the land of the Moabites, it returns here and also tells us the original inhabitants of the land of the Edomites, who were the Horims. But when God decided to give that land to the Edomites to dwell in, He allowed the sons of Esau, according to His eternal plan, to overcome them and dwell in their place, and so too He will give the land of Canaan to the children of Israel and drive out of it the pagans who inhabit the land.

2.7.2.en: Be faithful over all God's gifts to you so that He may bless you, but if you neglect them, God will take them from you and give them to one who deserves them.

2.8.s.en: (4) The perishing of the generation that came out of Egypt

2.8.0.en: The brook Zered: the Zered is a small river that rises from Mount Abarim east of the Dead Sea and flows into it; it marks the border between Edom and Moab and is now called "Wadi el-Hasa" (map 1).

2.8.1.en: The Lord guided the people at every step of their way toward the Promised Land, so when they reached that point after safely passing through the lands of the Edomites and the Moabites, the Lord asked them to rise up and cross the brook Zered.

2.9.0.en: The period that had passed since they left "Kadesh" was thirty-eight years, during which all the men of the generation that disobeyed the Lord by refusing to enter the land died.

2.9.1.en: Then they returned to Kadesh-barnea and crossed the Zered River; for their first coming to Kadesh-barnea was in the second year after their departure from Egypt, and they wandered in the wilderness of Sinai 38 years, then returned to Kadesh-barnea in the fortieth year after their departure from Egypt, where Aaron died in the fifth month, and then they crossed the Zered River (Num 33:38).

2.10.0.en: The camp: the place where the tents of the children of Israel are pitched.

2.10.1.en: The death of the men from twenty years old and upward was not due to old age alone, but the wrath of God came upon them and destroyed many of them, such as the death of the ten spies who spread murmuring among the people (Num 14:36, 37), and such as the death of Korah, Dathan, Abiram and the two hundred and fifty with them, whom the earth swallowed (Num 16); and a great number of them also died by the plague (Num 25:9).

2.10.2.en: The disobedience of the children of Israel to God's word deprived them of entering the Promised Land; so do not refuse to obey God's commandments because your mind rejects them or they conflict with your desires, lest you deprive yourself of happiness and of obtaining the Kingdom of Heaven.

2.11.s.en: (5) Not attacking the children of Ammon

2.11.0.en: When the generation that disobeyed the Lord had perished, the people were about to pass by the border of the land of Moab, passing through the city of "Ar," which is near the northern border of the land of Moab. The country of the children of Ammon lies north-west of the land of Moab (map 14).

2.11.1.en: Sea of Tiberias Yarmuk The Great Sea Jordan River Gilead Canaan Jabbok ● Heshbon Jahaz● ● Kedemoth A map showing the locations Aroer● Arnon ● taken by Sihon king of Heshbon from Ar Wadi Zered map (14)

2.12.0.en: Here too He warns them against showing enmity to the Ammonites or attacking them, because they are their kin and God gave them this land and will not allow the children of Israel to take it from them, for they are the sons of Lot, the son of their forefather Abraham's brother, by his younger daughter (Gen 19:38).

2.13.0.en: The Zamzummims: another name for the Rephaims; the Moabites call the Rephaims Emims, and the Ammonites call the Rephaims Zamzummims.

2.13.1.en: In truth the Emims and the Zamzummims are peoples branching from the Rephaims. The Zamzummims are also called the Zuzims, whom Chedorlaomer defeated (Gen 14:5). The meaning of the name Zamzummims is the "murmurers." Just as the book gave us the names of the original inhabitants of the land of Moab and the land of Edom, it tells us here the original inhabitants of the land of the children of Ammon. The Rephaims dwelt in it formerly, and it describes them as a strong people and likens them in their multitude and tallness to the Anakims mentioned in (v. 10). But God gave the children of Ammon victory over them and gave them their land.

2.14.0.en: Likewise God drove out the Horims, the original inhabitants of the land, from before the sons of Esau and made them dwell in their place.

2.14.1.en: God drives out the wicked and settles others in their place. If God blesses you, do not be proud, but thank Him and be humble before Him, for if you do evil the wrath of God will come upon you unless you repent.

2.15.0.en: The Avims: an ancient people who dwelt in the region of Gaza.

2.15.1.en: To confirm the driving out of the wicked peoples and the settling of others in their place, the book here mentions other invaders, the Caphtorims (the ancestors of the Philistines), who are the descendants of Mizraim the son of Ham the son of Noah (Gen 10:14). They came from the island of Crete (Caphtor) or from the Delta of Egypt, which is called (Kaft-Hor), and defeated the original inhabitants of the region of Gaza, who were the Avims. The Lord does not mention here that it was He who gave the Philistines this land, and consequently we find in (Josh 15:47) that this land was assigned to the tribe of Judah along with the rest of the cities of the south (Judg 18:1). God mentioned in this passage the driving out of peoples and the settling of peoples in their place in order to encourage the children of Israel, before whom He will drive out the wicked pagan peoples living in the land of Canaan.

2.16.0.en: The Amorites: a people who spoke a Semitic language, and it is mentioned in (Gen 10:16) that their lineage goes back to Canaan.

2.16.1.en: The valley of Arnon: it lies between the Arnon River, which flows into the middle of the Dead Sea on the east, and the Jabbok River, which rises near the present city of Amman and flows into the middle of the Jordan River on the east. This valley, or group of valleys of the Arnon, belonged to the Amorites before the children of Israel took it; the land of Moab lies south of the Arnon River.

2.16.2.en: Heshbon: the capital of the Amorites, where their king Sihon lived (Num 21:25, 27) (map 14). The Lord continues His leadership of the march of the children of Israel, who had crossed the lands of Moab, Edom and the children of Ammon without stirring up wars against them. And after encouraging them by mentioning the driving out of the ancient peoples and the dwelling of other peoples in their place, He commands them to advance, crossing the valley of Arnon in the direction of the kingdom of Sihon the Amorite, whose command center was the city of "Heshbon." The Lord declares to them that the stage of their taking possession of the lands begins now, and that they must declare war on Sihon. This is the first time that God asks them to fight the pagan inhabitants of the land to take possession of their land, for He had not previously approved of their attacking these inhabitants when they advanced of their own will without God's permission after the spies spied out the land of Canaan 38 years ago, and they were defeated and a great number of them were killed (Num 14:45). The evils of the Amorites were now complete and the time had come for God's wrath to fall on them, for God had said long ago to Abraham, "for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full" (Gen 15:16).

2.17.0.en: God reassures them that He will cast dread upon the inhabitants and kings of those lands which they will possess, so that they will be troubled and alarmed whenever they hear of the approach of the children of Israel to their country.

2.17.1.en: Here we see that the children of Israel had to fight and strive to possess the land, for it would not be granted to them without effort on their part; but the Lord would not leave them alone in the field, but would be in their midst, granting them victory.

2.17.2.en: We too must strive in our spiritual warfare against the enemy of good, for spiritual striving is a road on which everyone who seeks the Kingdom walks. We must always arm ourselves with spiritual vigilance to beware of the snares and works of Satan, but victory will not be ours except by the Lord's support of us in our striving, which frightens our enemies, so that the opponent collapses before us and the presence of the Lord is manifested in the midst of His beloved.

2.18.0.en: Kedemoth: a city east of the Dead Sea lying in the course of the valley of Arnon; it is now called Qasr el-Zafaran (map 14).

2.18.1.en: The wilderness of Kedemoth: the desert surrounding the city of Kedemoth.

2.18.2.en: Words of peace: Moses asked of Sihon the same thing he had asked before of the Edomites, the Moabites and the Ammonites, and assured him that he would not take anything from him by force, but that if he needed anything he would buy it from him with money, that is, he would not take anything from him without paying its price (Num 21:21, 22). The action of Moses here in sending messengers to Heshbon with words of peace may raise the question of the reason, and the answer is that this was done by inspiration from God in order to show the hardness that was in Sihon's heart and his not responding to the call of peace, so that he added evils to his evils and deserved to be crushed by God before the warriors of the children of Israel. What God allowed to happen to Sihon and to other peoples who met the same fate was not because God loved the children of Israel at the expense of those peoples; rather, what befell them was the natural fruit of the evils which those nations had committed.

2.19.0.en: I will go along by the highway, the highway: that is, I will go in a single line from which I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.

2.19.1.en: Moses asked to walk in a straight line without deviation, and if he needed anything he would buy it with money.

2.20.0.en: He reminds him that he had acted in this way before with the Ammonites and the Moabites and had not broken his promise, but Sihon refused, and what was in his heart of evil and hardness appeared.

2.21.0.en: As the Lord promised Moses, His promise was fulfilled, for He gave the children of Israel victory over Sihon and his army. And He says, "Begin to possess": for this was the first land they would possess in Canaan.

2.22.0.en: Jahaz: a Moabite city between the Arnon and the Jabbok, about 20 km east of the Dead Sea (map 14). Sihon came out to fight the children of Israel at the city of Jahaz; and Sihon, his sons and all his people were killed in the battle, so they no longer existed.

2.23.2.en: The children of Israel took all the cities of his kingdom and destroyed in every city all its inhabitants, men, women and children; no one escaped destruction and nothing escaped devastation.

2.24.0.en: The spoil of war which the children of Israel took from all the cities of the Amorites was the sheep and all the valuable possessions such as silver and gold.

2.25.0.en: Aroer: a Moabite city to the north of the Arnon River; it is also called Ar (v. 18). It is now called "Ara'ir."

2.25.1.en: The city that is in the valley: probably Heshbon, the capital of the Amorites.

2.25.2.en: Gilead: a mountainous region east of the Jordan River (map 14).

2.26.0.en: There was not one city too strong for us: we took possession of all the land of the Amorites.

2.26.1.en: The cities in the mountains: the mountainous region at the sources of the Jabbok River, which the Ammonites inhabited. The region which the children of Israel occupied was defined, from Aroer to Gilead. Moses affirms here that he did not touch the region of the children of Ammon adjoining those regions, in the valley of the Jabbok and the cities in the mountains and all the regions belonging to the peoples whom the Lord commanded them not to attack.

2.26.2.en: The victory over the king of Bashan and the division of the land east of the Jordan
